about.title: Campbell Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Campbell residents rely on a mix of local clinics, urgent care centers, and larger Santa Clara County medical systems for everything from routine care to surgery. Most of the time, that care goes as expected. But when a diagnosis is missed, a medication is dosed incorrectly, or a surgical step is rushed, the consequences can follow a patient for years. California law sets a narrow window and specific procedural steps for pursuing these claims, which makes early legal guidance especially valuable. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly — we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney in our network who focuses on medical injury claims and can walk you through whether what happened to you may qualify. If you or a family member in Campbell were harmed during treatment and are unsure what your options look like, reaching out early can help preserve records and timelines while things are still fresh.

items.title: We Understand the MICRA Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to act. An attorney in our network can help you figure out where you stand before that window closes.

items.title: Familiarity With the 90-Day Notice Rule
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider typically must receive 90 days' written notice. Missing this step can delay or complicate a claim, so early connection with an attorney matters.

items.title: Access to Attorneys Who Work With Medical Experts
items.desc: California law generally requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim, since a poor outcome alone isn't proof of negligence. We connect you with attorneys who know how to build that kind of case properly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Campbell?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider before a lawsuit can move forward. Because these deadlines can overlap in confusing ways, it helps to talk to an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is every bad medical outcome considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, so a poor result by itself isn't enough to prove negligence. A claim typically needs a qualified medical expert to show the provider's care fell below an accepted standard. An independent attorney can help you understand whether your situation meets that bar.

items.question: Are there limits on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: Yes — California caps non-economic damages (like pain and suffering) in malpractice claims, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic losses, such as medical bills and lost income, aren't subject to that same cap. An attorney can walk you through how this applies to a claim tied to care received in Campbell or elsewhere in Santa Clara County.
